text.arabic_uthmani: وَلَقَدْ هَمَّتْ بِهِۦ ۖ وَهَمَّ بِهَا لَوْلَآ أَن رَّءَا بُرْهَٰنَ رَبِّهِۦ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ لِنَصْرِفَ عَنْهُ ٱلسُّوٓءَ وَٱلْفَحْشَآءَ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ

words.gloss_range: resumptive and oath-adjacent conjunction opening the emphatic disclosure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: directed pre-action resolve; actualized as inner intention but not lexicalized as completed action

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the ayah as a resumptive entry into the locked-room scene (12:23), but it is already joined to the following certification frame. The reader is prepared to receive the coming desire report as asserted disclosure, and the clipped opening cadence moves quickly into the pressure of {{ar:هَمَّتْ}} ({{tr:hammat}}).

topics.headline: resumptive emphatic launch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not merely continue the scene; it opens the hidden desire report inside a strengthened certification frame.
topics.reason: The opening particle is read with the following assertion stack, so it resumes the scene while raising the first desire clause into certified narration.

topics.headline: clipped launch into pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the short opening cadence move into the doubled pressure of the first resolve verb.
topics.reason: The sound row adds a local acoustic payoff that supports, without replacing, the grammatical assertion frame.

words.gloss_range: emphatic lām inside the assertion frame before a perfect verb
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) is the emphatic element inside the opening frame, so the hidden inner event is presented with truth-force before the first lexical verb arrives. Its scope reaches the paired desire report: the second movement will be qualified by prevention, but the assertion frame is not erased.

topics.headline: lām intensifies hidden-event truth
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that interior desire is presented as verified narrative knowledge, not as conjecture.
topics.reason: The particle belongs to the fused opening assertion frame before a perfect verb and gives force to the hidden event even before later qualification.

words.gloss_range: certitude particle actualizing the following perfect while joining the opening certification frame

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: directed pre-action resolve; actualized as inner intention but not lexicalized as completed action

words.prose: {{ar:قَدْ}} ({{tr:qad}}) completes the opening certification package before {{ar:هَمَّتْ}} ({{tr:hammat}}), actualizing the first resolve as a narrated datum rather than a possibility. It also links this sensitive certification to the surah's earlier certifying frame (12:7), while its sound-near relation to later shirt-evidence scenes (12:26-28) remains echo pressure rather than the local function of the particle.

topics.headline: certitude actualizes the first resolve
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first resolve is linguistically actualized while still remaining an inner event rather than an outward act.
topics.reason: The particle before the perfect verb completes the opening certification frame and prevents the desire report from being reduced to mere possibility.

topics.headline: sound-near evidence echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices both a certifying-frame link to 12:7 and a sound-near link to later proof scenes (12:26-28), while the local particle remains a certitude marker rather than the torn-shirt root.
topics.reason: The q-d-d echo rows are useful as same-surah evidence pressure (12:7; 12:26-28), but they do not change the local function of the certitude particle.

words.gloss_range: directed pre-action resolve; actualized as inner intention but not lexicalized as completed action
words.root_gloss_range: root field of intention, concern, resolve, and inward preoccupation; local grammar selects directed pre-action resolve

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: directed pre-action resolve in the masculine clause; real inner movement constrained by the prevention clause

words.prose: {{ar:هَمَّتْ}} ({{tr:hammat}}) names serious inward resolve from {{ar:ه م م}} ({{tr:h-m-m}}), not completed outward action. The governed target phrase keeps the movement directed toward Yusuf, while the matching later {{ar:هَمَّ}} ({{tr:hamma}}) makes the two clauses a visible mirror - her toward him, then him toward her - before only the second half is interrupted.

topics.headline: actualized but pre-action resolve
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that her resolve is real and directed toward him, yet the verb-plus-preposition frame stops short of naming completed action.
topics.reason: Perfect aspect, resolve semantics, and the governed prepositional target together define a serious inner movement rather than execution.

topics.headline: mirrored resolve with compressed sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first resolve is built to mirror Yusuf's clause, so mutual pressure is staged before the second half is interrupted.
topics.reason: Form, local reprise, chiasm rows, and gemination rows converge on a verbal-pronominal mirror with audible pressure.

words.gloss_range: prepositional target phrase routing the first resolve toward Yusuf by pronoun

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: prepositional target phrase routing Yusuf's resolve toward the woman by pronoun

words.prose: {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihi}}) fuses the preposition with a masculine suffix, making Yusuf the target of her resolve without renaming him. It also completes the first half of the pronoun chiasm that will reverse in {{ar:بِهَا}} ({{tr:bihā}}).

topics.headline: masculine target in the first mirror half
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Yusuf is present as the directed target by suffix, while the preposition keeps him from being cast as a direct object of completed action.
topics.reason: The fused preposition-plus-pronoun supplies governance, target reference, pronoun continuity, and the first half of the target chiasm.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction that pairs the two desire clauses before the interruption

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: prevention particle making the sight of proof the condition that blocks completion

words.prose: The second {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) coordinates the two resolve clauses under the live assertion frame. That coordination creates parity first, so the later {{ar:لَوْلَآ}} ({{tr:lawlā}}) can rupture only Yusuf's side and turn symmetry into meaningful asymmetry.

topics.headline: coordination creates parity before rupture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second desire clause is joined as a real counterpart before the prevention particle makes the asymmetry meaningful.
topics.reason: The conjunction links the two resolve clauses under the active assertion frame, while later grammar differentiates only the second clause.

words.gloss_range: directed pre-action resolve in the masculine clause; real inner movement constrained by the prevention clause
words.root_gloss_range: root field of intention, concern, resolve, and inward preoccupation; local grammar selects real but interrupted pre-action resolve

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: prevention particle making the sight of proof the condition that blocks completion

words.prose: {{ar:هَمَّ}} ({{tr:hamma}}) must be read as the surface verb from {{ar:ه م م}} ({{tr:h-m-m}}) despite the tag anomaly in the bundle. It acknowledges a real inner resolve and pressure, but {{ar:لَوْلَآ}} ({{tr:lawlā}}) and the proof clause make that movement intercepted rather than completed; the prior scene (12:23) supplies the threatened completion without spelling it out here.

topics.headline: surface is verb despite tag anomaly
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the local reading must follow the surface verb and its prepositional target, not the bundle's anomalous pronoun tag.
topics.reason: The surface sequence and following complement require a 3ms perfect verb; the tag anomaly is a guardrail issue, not the local parse.

topics.headline: real resolve interrupted by proof
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Yusuf's inner movement is acknowledged before the proof clause blocks its completion.
topics.reason: The perfect verb, shared h-m-m pressure, and later prevention clause together create a real-but-intercepted inner movement.

topics.headline: prior scene becomes inner resolve
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the previous solicitation supplies the pressure-field in which Yusuf's inner resolve is named and then stopped.
topics.reason: Boundary and intertext rows tie the clause to 12:23 and explain why the prevented completion is recoverable without being spelled out.

words.gloss_range: prepositional target phrase routing Yusuf's resolve toward the woman by pronoun

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: prepositional target phrase routing the first resolve toward Yusuf by pronoun

words.prose: {{ar:بِهَا}} ({{tr:bihā}}) mirrors {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihi}}) with the same preposition and the opposite gendered suffix. The woman is carried as target by pronoun, so the ayah stages reciprocal direction while still keeping both actors unnamed in this clause pair.

topics.headline: feminine target completes the mirror
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same preposition now carries the opposite gendered suffix, completing the reciprocal target pattern without naming either actor.
topics.reason: Governance, pronoun fusion, antecedent continuity, and chiasm rows all point to the second half of the pronominal mirror.

words.gloss_range: prevention particle making the sight of proof the condition that blocks completion
words.prose: {{ar:لَوْلَآ}} ({{tr:lawlā}}) is the hinge where mirrored resolve becomes prevention. It requires both a threatened continuation and an existing barrier, so the seeing of proof becomes the grammatical condition that stops the forward movement.

topics.headline: prevention turns symmetry into interruption
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the mirrored desire sequence is not flat mutuality; this particle turns the second half into a blocked counterfactual.
topics.reason: The particle requires a preventing condition and makes the seeing of proof the barrier that changes the direction of the clause.

words.gloss_range: subordinating/nominalizing particle making the seeing clause function as the preventive condition

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: prevention particle making the sight of proof the condition that blocks completion

words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) turns the following seeing clause into a substantive condition after {{ar:لَوْلَآ}} ({{tr:lawlā}}). The result is that Yusuf's seeing of the proof is not a side event but the thing whose existence blocks completion.

topics.headline: seeing becomes the preventive condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sight of proof is made grammatically substantive, the thing whose existence blocks completion.
topics.reason: The particle nominalizes the following perfect verb phrase so it can stand as the condition governed by the prevention particle.

words.gloss_range: perception of proof, left open between optical sight and cognitive apprehension but locally transitive
words.root_gloss_range: root field of seeing, perceiving, and judgment-forming apprehension; local object narrows it to proof-perception
words.prose: {{ar:رَّءَا}} ({{tr:raʾā}}) governs the proof as its object, making the interruption an encounter with evidence rather than a vague impulse. The verb can cover sight and judgment-forming apprehension, and the ayah leaves that channel open while keeping the local frame transitive and proof-focused; it also joins Surah Yusuf's wider vision thread from 12:4 through evidence and recognition scenes (12:28; 12:43; 12:100). Against overwhelming divine-manifestation seeing elsewhere (7:143), this proof-seeing preserves Yusuf by stopping the harmful trajectory.

topics.headline: proof is the object seen
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the interruption is not a vague feeling; the verb takes proof as its explicit object.
topics.reason: Local grammar gives the perception verb one accusative proof-object inside the nominalized prevention clause.

topics.headline: sight and apprehension remain open
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah centers evidentiary perception while withholding whether that perception is optical, cognitive, or both.
topics.reason: The root and form allow sight and judgment-forming perception, but the local object narrows the claim to proof-perception rather than unbounded mental activity.

topics.headline: vision redirects the Yusuf story
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this seeing belongs to Surah Yusuf's wider vision-and-evidence pattern (12:4; 12:28; 12:43; 12:100) and contrasts with destructive divine-manifestation seeing (7:143), because here vision prevents action and preserves Yusuf.
topics.reason: Same-surah and cross-reference rows connect this seeing with dream vision (12:4), shirt proof (12:28), royal dream vision (12:43), final recognition (12:100), and the contrastive preservation-against-destruction scene (7:143), while local grammar keeps it protective.

words.gloss_range: clarifying proof as the perceived object, sourced through the construct relation to his Lord and not described in content
words.root_gloss_range: proof and manifest demonstration field; local construct makes it a Lord-sourced proof rather than a generic argument
words.prose: {{ar:بُرْهَٰنَ}} ({{tr:burhāna}}) is the object seen and the construct head of the Lord-sourced proof phrase. The word carries manifest-proof force, but the content is deliberately withheld: the reader knows what the proof does and whose it is, not what it looked like. Its wider proof-formula field is inverted here: against challenge or public-proof formulas (2:111; 21:24; 28:32; 4:174), Yusuf receives proof instead of being challenged to produce it.

topics.headline: Lord-sourced proof object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proof is both what Yusuf sees and what belongs to his Lord, so the interruption is sourced rather than self-generated.
topics.reason: Object grammar and construct-state grammar join perception to the Lord-source in one proof phrase.

topics.headline: clear proof with withheld content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proof is forceful and manifest, while the text refuses to identify its visible content.
topics.reason: The lexical proof field, nominal form, rarity, and deliberate omission preserve function and source without importing later narrative supplements.

topics.headline: received proof instead of demanded proof
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a Quranic proof term used in challenge or public-proof formulas (2:111; 21:24; 28:32; 4:174) is turned here into a protective proof given to Yusuf.
topics.reason: Intertext rows contrast demanded proof (2:111; 21:24), public divine proof (28:32; 4:174), and the received proof of 12:24, with the local ayah making proof a personal protective object.

words.gloss_range: possessed Lord-title sourcing the proof through Yusuf's personal Lord-relation
words.root_gloss_range: lordship, ownership, sustaining, and cultivation field; local suffix makes it Yusuf's Lord-relation
words.prose: {{ar:رَبِّهِۦ}} ({{tr:rabbihi}}) closes the proof phrase by tying the proof to Yusuf's own Lord-relation. The title carries governance and cultivation, so the proof reads as protective Lordship; it also anticipates the later protection chain around Yusuf's plea and response in 12:33-34 and belongs to the wider Lordship-governs-indecency field seen in 7:33.

topics.headline: his Lord sources the proof
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proof is not merely divine in abstraction; it is tied to Yusuf's own Lord-relation.
topics.reason: The genitive construct tail and suffix make the Lord the possessor/source of the proof, not the object seen.

topics.headline: Lordship as cultivation and governance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the title frames the proof as nurturing governance, not only command or prohibition.
topics.reason: The root field of lordship, ownership, sustaining, and cultivation remains locally relevant because the proof guides Yusuf away from harm.

topics.headline: Lord relation links refusal, proof, and later averting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a Lordship thread running through the crisis and later protection scenes (12:33-34), with the same Lordship field governing indecency in 7:33.
topics.reason: Same-surah and co-occurrence rows connect the Lord-source of proof with Yusuf's later plea (12:33), the answer using protection vocabulary (12:34), and Lordship over indecency in 7:33.

words.gloss_range: comparison/manner prefix that turns the prior event into the manner of divine action
words.prose: {{ar:كَ}} ({{tr:ka}}) supplies the manner force in the pivot expression: the preceding interruption is treated as the way divine action works. The ayah turns from event-report to method-explanation before the purpose clause names the aim.

topics.headline: comparison turns event into method
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah shifts from narrated event to divine method: in that way, the averting purpose is explained.
topics.reason: The prefix supplies manner/comparison force inside the pivot expression before the purpose clause.

words.gloss_range: distal demonstrative packaging the prior sequence as the referent explained by the purpose clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: comparison/manner prefix that turns the prior event into the manner of divine action

words.prose: {{ar:ذَلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhālika}}) compresses the whole prior chain of desire, prevention, seeing, and proof into one backward pointer. In the fused expression with {{ar:كَ}} ({{tr:ka}}), that pointer becomes the event-as-method that the following purpose clause explains.

topics.headline: prior chain becomes one pointer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the whole desire-proof-interruption sequence is compressed into a single demonstrative before its purpose is named.
topics.reason: The demonstrative, fused with comparison, packages the prior event as the object of divine explanation.

words.gloss_range: purpose lām attaching the divine rationale to the following subjunctive verb

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: divine first-person purposeful turning away; direct redirection from Yusuf of the named harms
possessed Lord-title sourcing the proof through Yusuf's personal Lord-relation

words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) attaches purpose directly to {{ar:نَصْرِفَ}} ({{tr:naṣrifa}}). It makes the proof-interruption intentional divine action, opening the shift from third-person narration about {{ar:رَبِّهِۦ}} ({{tr:rabbihi}}) into the divine first-person rationale.

topics.headline: purpose lām opens divine rationale
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proof-interruption is not accidental help; the grammar states it as purposeful divine action.
topics.reason: The attached purpose particle governs the following subjunctive and introduces the divine first-person purpose register.

words.gloss_range: divine first-person purposeful turning away; direct redirection from Yusuf of the named harms
words.root_gloss_range: turning, redirecting, averting, and dismissal field; local frame selects protective turning away from Yusuf
words.prose: {{ar:نَصْرِفَ}} ({{tr:naṣrifa}}) voices the purpose as divine first-person averting: God turns the named harms away from Yusuf. The root image from {{ar:ص ر ف}} ({{tr:ṣ-r-f}}) makes protection feel like redirected trajectory, and the same protection verb becomes a Surah Yusuf thread in 12:33-34. Variant agency evidence sharpens the issue because a third-person singular reading would shift the surface toward He or it averts, but the local surface keeps direct divine agency primary. Against judgmental turning-away scenes such as 7:146 and 9:127, this clause is the protective pole: evil is turned away from the servant.

topics.headline: variant exposes agency pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that variant evidence can shift the surface toward a third-person singular He/it averts reading, while the local canonical surface makes direct divine first-person agency primary.
topics.reason: The variant can illuminate agency pressure, but it does not replace the local first-person plural verb governed by the purpose particle.

topics.headline: divine We states purposeful averting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the intervention is voiced as divine agency and dependent purpose, not as a detached past comment.
topics.reason: The first-person prefix, subjunctive mood, purpose governance, and Form I shape make the action direct and intentional.

topics.headline: protection as redirected trajectory
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that protection is pictured as turning a harmful trajectory away from Yusuf, the protective inverse of judgmental turning-away scenes such as 7:146 and 9:127.
topics.reason: Root semantics and the argument frame assign God as redirection agent, Yusuf as beneficiary, and the two harms as objects turned away.

topics.headline: ṣarf protection thread begins here
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this verb opens a Surah Yusuf protection chain replayed in 12:33-34, while also contrasting with judgmental uses of divine turning away elsewhere (7:146; 9:127).
topics.reason: Intertext and boundary rows connect the purpose verb to Yusuf's later plea (12:33), answer language (12:34), and inverse judgmental ṣarf scenes (7:146; 9:127).

topics.headline: rationale beat links proof to status
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this clause is the ayah's rationale beat, connecting desire, proof, averted harms, final status, and the target-reversal of divine turning away seen against 9:127.
topics.reason: Structural and synthesis rows show the four-beat movement from desire to interruption to divine purpose to closing classification, while 9:127 supplies the inverse target pattern for divine turning away.

words.gloss_range: separation phrase marking Yusuf as beneficiary of the averting

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: definite broad harm term, first object of the divine averting and paired with specific indecency
definite abstract term for extreme indecency, second object of the divine averting

words.prose: {{ar:عَنْهُ}} ({{tr:ʿanhu}}) defines the direction of the averting: the harms are turned away from him. Its position before the objects foregrounds Yusuf as beneficiary before {{ar:ٱلسُّوٓءَ}} ({{tr:al-sūʾa}}) and {{ar:وَٱلْفَحْشَآءَ}} ({{tr:wa-l-faḥshāʾa}}) are named.

topics.headline: away-from-him protects Yusuf
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Yusuf is placed before the named harms as the beneficiary from whom they are turned away.
topics.reason: The separation preposition and suffix define the direction of the divine redirection and carry Yusuf by pronoun through the clause.

words.gloss_range: definite broad harm term, first object of the divine averting and paired with specific indecency
words.root_gloss_range: evil, harm, ugliness, calamity, and disgrace field; local pairing keeps broad harm before specific indecency

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: definite abstract term for extreme indecency, second object of the divine averting

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلسُّوٓءَ}} ({{tr:al-sūʾa}}) is the first object God averts, a definite broad harm term rather than an accusation against Yusuf. It opens the object pair broadly before {{ar:وَٱلْفَحْشَآءَ}} ({{tr:wa-l-faḥshāʾa}}) narrows the danger; the harm is under divine governance, contrasting with harm God wills for a people in 13:11, and the same vocabulary later belongs to the surah's accusation and exoneration arc (12:25; 12:51; 12:53).

topics.headline: definite first object of averting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the broad harm term is the first object God turns away, not an attribute of Yusuf.
topics.reason: The definite accusative object is governed by the averting verb and starts the coordinated harm pair.

topics.headline: broad harm precedes specific indecency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the protection covers more than sexual transgression: the whole harmful outcome-field is named first.
topics.reason: The root field includes evil, harm, ugliness, calamity, and disgrace; paired order makes it broad before the narrower second term.

topics.headline: averted harm anticipates accusation and testimony
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the harm term is governed by divine direction: paired with indecency here, contrasted with harm willed for a people in 13:11, and later re-entering accusation and exoneration scenes (12:25; 12:51; 12:53).
topics.reason: Cross-reference and boundary rows connect the averted harm here with the paired moral field, the contrastive divine-will scene (13:11), the accusation field (12:25), later testimony (12:51), and internal reckoning (12:53).

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction preserving the second harm term as a distinct object
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps the two averted objects coordinated under one verb. The reader should not collapse the second noun into a restatement of the first: broad evil and extreme indecency remain distinct targets of the same divine redirection.

topics.headline: connector preserves two averted objects
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that broad evil and extreme indecency remain distinct coordinated targets under one divine act.
topics.reason: The conjunction governs the second object under the same verb while preventing the second noun from collapsing into an apposition.

words.gloss_range: definite abstract term for extreme indecency, second object of the divine averting
words.root_gloss_range: excessive ugliness and indecency field; local definite abstract form selects the known severe moral category

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: divine first-person purposeful turning away; direct redirection from Yusuf of the named harms
definite broad harm term, first object of the divine averting and paired with specific indecency

words.prose: {{ar:وَٱلْفَحْشَآءَ}} ({{tr:wa-l-faḥshāʾa}}) names the specific, scene-known category of severe indecency as a second object of {{ar:نَصْرِفَ}} ({{tr:naṣrifa}}). It completes the broad-to-specific pair with {{ar:ٱلسُّوٓءَ}} ({{tr:al-sūʾa}}), and the same evil-and-indecency ordering is reversed from satanic command into divine averting when compared with 2:169.

topics.headline: specific extreme indecency is averted
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second object names the scene-specific category of severe indecency, not just a synonym for broad harm.
topics.reason: Definiteness, accusative coordination, abstract form, and lexical scope make the term an independently averted moral category.

topics.headline: satanic command pair is reversed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a recognized evil-and-indecency pair appears here under divine averting rather than under satanic command, especially against 2:169.
topics.reason: Intertext rows show the same moral pair and order in other passages, while 12:24 reverses its direction into protection.

words.gloss_range: emphatic closing particle-plus-pronoun certifying Yusuf's status
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّهُۥ}} ({{tr:innahu}}) opens the final certification clause and carries Yusuf by pronoun into the closing verdict. The ayah therefore ends not on desire or proof alone, but on emphatic divine attestation of his status.

topics.headline: emphatic final status verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah's last movement is certified classification, not the desire scene itself.
topics.reason: The emphatic particle with masculine pronoun carries Yusuf into the final status clause and bookends the opening certification frame.

words.gloss_range: partitive preposition placing Yusuf among a class rather than equating him with the whole class
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) makes the closing predicate partitive: Yusuf is from among a class. That small preposition starts the narrowing sequence from membership to possessed servants to the final purification status.

topics.headline: from among a class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Yusuf is located within a recognized servant class rather than described as an isolated moral exception.
topics.reason: The partitive preposition governs the servant phrase and begins a narrowing sequence from membership to qualified purification.

words.gloss_range: plural possessed servant-class, governed by the partitive and qualified by the final participle
words.root_gloss_range: service, worship, and devoted subjection field; local plural possessive selects divine servant-belonging

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: divine first-person purposeful turning away; direct redirection from Yusuf of the named harms

words.prose: {{ar:عِبَادِنَا}} ({{tr:ʿibādinā}}) places Yusuf among a plural, divinely possessed servant class. Its possessive suffix links the servants to the same divine speaker of {{ar:نَصْرِفَ}} ({{tr:naṣrifa}}), while the root field from {{ar:ع ب د}} ({{tr:ʿ-b-d}}) makes the status devoted belonging under God. The phrase also joins protected-servant and exclusive-worship formulas, including 12:40, 15:40, and 17:65, while pairing servanthood with the Lordship frame of proof and protection.

topics.headline: collective divine servant-belonging
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Yusuf belongs among God's possessed servant class, with the same divine speaker who averts claiming the servants as Our own.
topics.reason: Genitive governance, plural form, possessive suffix, and modifier relation make the closing class collective, possessed, and bound to purification.

topics.headline: servanthood as devoted subjection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the closing status is devoted belonging under God, not generic moral respectability or mere self-control.
topics.reason: The root field of service, worship, and subjection remains active through the possessed servant phrase.

topics.headline: servant and purified form a recognized pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final phrase joins a broader protected-servant and exclusive-worship formula, with echoes such as 12:40, 15:40, and 17:65, while pairing servanthood with Lordship.
topics.reason: Co-occurrence, same-surah, and cross-reference rows connect servant language with purification, Lordship, exclusive worship (12:40), and protected status (15:40; 17:65).

words.gloss_range: definite plural Form IV participial status of being made pure or selected, with active/passive reading pressure noted
words.root_gloss_range: purity, exclusivity, deliverance, and being set apart; local passive participial reading emphasizes caused purification
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمُخْلَصِينَ}} ({{tr:al-mukhlaṣīn}}) is the ayah's final seal: Yusuf belongs among the definite purified ones. The passive reading makes purification received and caused, not self-achieved, while variant evidence keeps the active-sincerity contrast visible. The root field adds being set apart and delivered into purified belonging, and the ending connects the narrative crisis to a broader purified-servant category, including echoes such as 15:40, 19:51, 37:40, and 38:83, before later human selection language appears in 12:54.

topics.headline: active-passive vowel contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a small reading difference can shift the emphasis from servants being sincere to servants being made pure, while the local output keeps the passive purification reading primary.
topics.reason: Variant rows are retained for agency pressure, but the canonical passive participial reading governs the local prose.

topics.headline: definite final class seal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah ends by sealing Yusuf inside an identifiable purified-servant class, not with an unresolved crisis.
topics.reason: Agreement/apposition options, definite plural form, participial status, distribution, and closure position all make the final word a status seal.

topics.headline: caused purification and deliverance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that protection is reread as being set apart and delivered into purified belonging by another agent.
topics.reason: The root field and passive participle assign purification as caused and received rather than self-generated.

topics.headline: recognized protected category
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Yusuf's final designation participates in a broader purified-servant formula and prophetic status category, with echoes such as 15:40, 19:51, 37:40, and 38:83, and it precedes later human selection language in 12:54.
topics.reason: Intertext rows link the closing word with servant-purification formulas (15:40; 37:40; 38:83), prophetic designation (19:51), later royal selection language (12:54), and later same-surah root contrast (12:80).

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired هَمَّتْ and هَمَّ, the لَوْلَا clause, and the sequence of seeing proof followed by turning-away.
baseline_models.mechanism: Two inward orientations reach a narrated threshold, but perception of proof interrupts equivalence and divine redirection changes the trajectory before the intended relation becomes completed action.

activation_trace.role: The branch gives both mirrored verbs inwardly formed concern or resolve, making the threshold live rather than grammatically empty.
Sense or insight supplies the interrupting apprehension through which the scene is newly perceived.
Demonstrative proof gives the perception evidentiary force rather than leaving it a bare emotional recoil.
Turning something back from its face supplies the decisive change of direction away from the threatened outcome.

changed_reading.before: The verse is a flat contrast between her desire and his absence of desire.
changed_reading.after: The verse stages mirrored, genuinely formed orientation at a threshold, then marks the asymmetry as an interruption by apprehended proof and a redirected course.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: لِنَصْرِفَ عَنْهُ السُّوءَ وَالْفَحْشَاءَ and the closing description الْمُخْلَصِينَ.
baseline_models.mechanism: Protection is spatial and processual: evil and excess are turned off his path while he is purified from admixture and extracted from what could ensnare him. The objects are not necessarily identical; general harm, sexual exposure, and exceeded bounds remain layered.

activation_trace.role: Transfer from one state or course to another makes protection a rerouting process, not merely a verdict about character.
The concealed sexual or shame-bearing exposure sharpens one bodily and reputational layer of what is turned away.
Exceeding a proper limit makes the danger an escalation beyond measure, broader than one named act.
Purification after mixture supplies the selective clarification of the servant through contact with, not ignorance of, danger.
Escape after becoming caught supplies the rescue dimension, keeping chosen status compatible with a real snare.

changed_reading.before: Being chosen means possessing a static purity that prevents any real proximity to temptation.
changed_reading.after: Being chosen is disclosed as active extraction, rerouting, and clarification within a real field of harm and exceeded limits.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The proof is specifically بُرْهَانَ رَبِّهِ, and the explanation closes with مِنْ عِبَادِنَا الْمُخْلَصِينَ.
baseline_models.mechanism: The proof belongs to a lordly relation of ownership, repair, and staged formation. Servanthood supplies responsive obedience, while chosen distinctness explains why the intervention belongs to an ongoing relation rather than an isolated visual event.

activation_trace.role: Gradual repair, nurture, and completion make the proof an act within continuing formation.
Obedience with humble service supplies the human response within that formative relation.
Selection and distinction from competing claims give the servant a particular belonging and orientation.
Established evidence functions as the timely medium through which formation becomes directive.

changed_reading.before: A detached sign suddenly suppresses an otherwise self-contained episode.
changed_reading.after: The seen proof is a timely act of an already formative lord-servant relation that repairs direction and confirms particular belonging.

context_deltas.mechanism: The pre-focus sequence moves Joseph through concealment, commodification, diminished valuation, honored lodging, empowerment, and corrective judgment. This makes chosen servanthood a capacity formed and preserved through alien ownership systems rather than an untouched essence outside them.

activation_trace.role: Purification after admixture anchors the claim that prior social handling can be traversed without defining the servant.
Hiding something inward supplies the first imposed concealment through which Joseph is handled.
A cut-off portion of wealth becoming merchandise supplies the objectifying economic frame.
Reduction from due worth makes the external valuation explicitly deficient.
Honorable generosity reverses the preceding deficient valuation without yet granting full autonomy.
Empowerment supplies a counter-current of granted capacity within the same land and household.
Preventive restraint for repair anticipates the focus verse's redirection as trained judgment.

structural_cues: 12:19-22 moves from concealed merchandise and diminished price to honored lodging, empowerment, maturity, judgment, and knowledge immediately before the focus scene.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies successive reversals of valuation and a grant of corrective judgment; I infer that these stages form preserved agency culminating in 12:24. A live alternative is that they establish biography and providence without specifying the mechanism of resistance.

changed_reading.before: الْمُخْلَصِينَ is only a timeless honorific attached after the event.
changed_reading.after: The title gathers a prior process in which external owners repeatedly redefine Joseph while lordly formation preserves and equips an agency not reducible to their valuations.

context_deltas.mechanism: Repeated solicitation is staged inside deliberately tightened architecture: doors are made fast, an imperative summons him, and he seeks refuge. The mirrored هَمَّ clauses therefore occur in an asymmetric field of pursuit, enclosure, and attempted refusal, while divine turning opens a direction unavailable in the closed room.

activation_trace.role: Formed inward orientation remains the focus anchor, but context changes the pressures under which each orientation forms.
Persistent solicitation toward an act supplies her directed pursuit rather than a merely simultaneous feeling.
Coercive tightening and constriction make the closure an exertion of control over the available courses.
The entryway image turns the room into a system of channels whose exits have been controlled.
An explicit summons supplies the verbal force pressing the encounter toward enactment.
Seeking refuge and protective attachment supplies Joseph's already stated counter-orientation.
Redirection away from a faced course functions as an opening in the otherwise narrowed choice-space.

structural_cues: 12:23 places solicitation, multiplied door-closing, summons, and refuge directly before the paired هَمَّ clauses.
The first narrated bodily movement after 12:24 is toward the door rather than toward the summoner.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies directed pursuit, controlled exits, summons, and refuge; I infer that the architecture makes the two intentions functionally unequal and that divine turning restores an exit-course. Alternatively, the enclosure may intensify the scene without altering the lexical force of his هَمَّ.

changed_reading.before: The paired verbs describe two isolated and freely symmetrical desires.
changed_reading.after: They are verbally mirrored but causally asymmetric: her sustained pursuit narrows the room, his live inward threshold occurs after refuge within that pressure, and the decisive change is a restored direction out.

context_deltas.mechanism: The inward turn becomes bodily flight; flight leaves a directional tear; the tear becomes a witnessed criterion; and sight later reads that criterion. The aftermath does not identify the earlier برهان, but it places it in a broader proof ecology where moral direction becomes material and legible.

activation_trace.role: Established demonstration anchors the focus event as proof-bearing rather than only affective.
A course turned away supplies the inward directional change that the following movement externalizes.
Advancing in a race supplies rapid opposed motion toward the exit.
The entryway becomes the concrete destination through which redirection is enacted and exposed.
A lengthwise tear supplies a durable material trace generated by the opposed movement.
The worn shirt is the body-adjacent surface that receives and preserves the trace.
Turning one's back gives the tear directional meaning as evidence of withdrawal.
A sign that bears witness converts the damaged garment from residue into an evidentiary criterion.
Front-facing orientation supplies the counterfactual direction against which the rear tear is tested.
Stable verification supplies the criterion's capacity to establish which account holds.
Later sight reads the physical sign, echoing the focus sequence of seeing and proof without equating the two objects.

structural_cues: 12:25 converts the focus redirection into a race to the door and a shirt torn from behind.
12:26-28 orders witness, front-versus-back testing, and sight of the rear tear as a public verification sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies outward flight, a directionally marked tear, and its later evidentiary reading; I infer that these externalize the moral vector of صَرْف and illuminate what proof does in the scene. The live alternative is that the focus برهان is a wholly distinct prior disclosure and the shirt only corroborates innocence afterward.

changed_reading.before: The seen proof is a private apparition whose effect leaves no inspectable relation to subsequent events.
changed_reading.after: The proof initiates a direction that becomes embodied in flight and later legible through a material witness, while the earlier and later proofs remain distinguishable.

context_deltas.mechanism: The danger expands from a closed encounter into a circuit of report, gaze, affect, and bodily injury. What is turned away from Joseph includes not only a proposed act but a spectacle that recruits other viewers and makes bodies bear the excess.

activation_trace.role: Shame-bearing sexual exposure anchors the reputational and bodily danger that can spread beyond the room.
Excess beyond proper measure supplies the category under which social fascination becomes bodily overrun.
Love reaching the heart's enclosing layer supplies an affect imagined as penetrating inward boundaries.
Love adhering to the heart supplies the persistent affect that public speech attributes to the encounter.
Report spreading among people supplies the social transmission that carries the private scene outward.
Direct sight supplies the activating gaze through which the reported desire is experimentally reproduced.
Severing and separation supply the literal bodily consequence of affect exceeding controlled measure.
The bodily hand localizes the injury, making the spectacle's harm visible rather than metaphorical.

structural_cues: 12:30-31 moves from city speech about desire to a staged viewing in which multiple women reproduce astonishment and cut their hands.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies public report, orchestrated sight, and bodily cutting; I infer that السوء والفحشاء can include a socially amplified economy of exposure and harm, not just a private sexual endpoint. Alternatively, the later spectacle may illustrate only Joseph's beauty and leave the focus objects narrowly moral.

changed_reading.before: السوء والفحشاء name one private act proposed by one woman.
changed_reading.after: They can also name the expanding system of exposure, contagious gaze, affective excess, and bodily damage from which Joseph's course is kept distinct.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later speech names his active holding-fast, renewed solicitation, coercive threat, acknowledged possibility of inclination, petition for turning, and received answer. Divine protection and human agency are therefore coupled, and chosen status does not erase vulnerability or dependence.

activation_trace.role: Rescue after entanglement anchors chosen status as deliverance compatible with genuine exposure.
The repeated solicitation confirms that the pressure persists after the focus rescue.
The inward faculty of mind and response identifies the contested site as personal agency, not only external movement.
Grasping that prevents and preserves supplies an active human form taken by protection.
Confinement supplies the coercive cost threatened against continued resistance.
Highest preference makes prison a consciously ranked cost rather than an accidental escape.
Calling that verbally inclines another supplies the continuing interpersonal pull against which aid is sought.
The focus verb reappears as requested redirection, converting the earlier explanation into an explicit dependence.
Inclination of the heart supplies the vulnerability Joseph himself treats as materially possible.
Disordered restraint and temperament supply the feared consequence of yielding, not merely missing information.
A returned answer closes the petition-response circuit and attributes effective aid to relation.
Actual redirection answers the requested turning and repeats the focus mechanism under widened pressure.

structural_cues: 12:32 joins confession of solicitation and self-restraint to a threat of prison and humiliation.
12:33 conditionally admits possible inclination unless God turns the women's pressure away, and 12:34 narrates response and turning.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies active self-restraint, costly preference, admitted possible inclination, petition, and answer; I infer that 12:24 describes relationally sustained protection rather than ontological invulnerability. Alternatively, 12:24 may narrate one completed rescue while 12:33-34 begins a separate rescue from collective pressure.

changed_reading.before: Divine turning cancels human agency and proves that a chosen servant cannot experience subsequent inclination.
changed_reading.after: Divine turning is enacted through holding-fast, costly choice, candid vulnerability, prayer, and response; chosenness secures relation and rescue, not effortless immunity.

context_deltas.mechanism: Visible signs can establish moral direction and still fail to control a household's institutional decision. The focus proof effectively redirects Joseph, but proof's efficacy must be separated from immediate release, vindication, or freedom from imposed consequences.

activation_trace.role: Demonstrative proof anchors the distinction between evidence's directive force and political enforcement.
Emergence into visibility supplies the public availability of what had become evident.
Perception of the signs echoes the focus act of seeing while shifting the viewers to the ruling household.
An outwardly manifest sign supplies evidence that is acknowledged before the contrary decision.
Confinement supplies the institutionally imposed outcome that visible evidence does not prevent.
A bounded interval makes the adverse consequence temporally real even if it is not final.

structural_cues: 12:35 explicitly sequences seeing the signs before deciding on imprisonment for a time.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies perceived signs followed by timed confinement; I infer that proof can succeed in redirecting the servant while failing to compel the powerful. Alternatively, the imprisonment may itself be another means by which harm is turned away, making institutional defeat simultaneously protective.

changed_reading.before: Seeing divine proof should remove danger, vindicate innocence, and prevent adverse consequences in the same register.
changed_reading.after: Proof redirects the moral course and can make truth visible without immediately defeating coercive power; even imprisonment may remain either harm or a second protective diversion.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the non-dominant ر د د mapping behind the context root ر و د rather than offering its ordinary parse. It remains packet-resolved and anchored to the focus صَرْف mechanism, so it is worth carrying as a latent counter-vector. Downstream prose should call it a split-root echo, not translate رَاوَدَتْ as repulsion.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus redirects a formed orientation away, while the immediately preceding solicitation has a packet-supplied alternate mapping whose branch pushes back and prevents.

activation_trace.role: Repelling and preventing supplies a latent inverse vector inside the mapped inventory of the pursuit cue.
Turning back from a faced course anchors that inverse vector in the focus verse's explicit action.

changed_reading.before: Solicitation and protection are only sequential, externally opposed events.
changed_reading.after: At the packet's split-root level, pursuit carries a shadow of return and repulsion, allowing the scene to be heard as competing vectors already folded around the threshold.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is form-distant because it uses the non-dominant ر و ي mapping for the QAC root ر ء ي. It remains anchored to رَأَى and explains how proof could alter an already formed هَمّ by restoring reflective interval. Downstream prose should present it as an abductive activation, not as the lexical replacement of seeing.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: رَأَى occurs precisely between the paired intentions and the explanatory divine turning.

activation_trace.role: Inwardly formed resolve supplies the state that requires interruption rather than mere information.
Deliberative consideration supplies a recovered pause in which the formed course can be reassessed.

changed_reading.before: Seeing the proof is an instantaneous visual shock acting independently of thought.
changed_reading.after: The sight may also activate recovered deliberation, widening a constricted instant enough for intention to be re-read and redirected.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This cross-domain model is surprising because it carries ه م م through melting and flow imagery rather than its primary intentional branch. It remains anchored to the repeated verb, explicit transposition in صَرْف, and subsequent race toward the door. Downstream prose should qualify it as a material analogy for activation dynamics, not a dictionary gloss.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The repeated هَمَّ supplies rising activation, and نَصْرِفَ explicitly changes its threatened course before the body races toward the exit.

activation_trace.role: Melting and movement after rigidity model intention as activation passing from held state toward flow.
Transfer between states or courses supplies the rerouting of that activation rather than its annihilation.
Rapid forward competition gives the rerouted activation a bodily outlet toward escape.

changed_reading.before: The episode switches desire off and replaces motion with stillness.
changed_reading.after: The episode may reroute already mobilized energy: incipient flow is not erased but converted into rapid flight from the threatened act.

strongest_changes: The mirrored هَمَّ clauses remain real but cease to be causally symmetrical once solicitation, enclosure, refuge, proof, and restored exit-direction are integrated.
الْمُخْلَصِينَ shifts from static immunity to extraction, formed agency, and relationally sustained rescue within genuine vulnerability.
The torn shirt and its directional reading do not identify the focus برهان, but they reveal a proof ecology in which inward redirection becomes bodily and publicly legible.
The later repetition of صَرْف as petition and answer makes protection a coupled process of restraint, costly choice, admitted susceptibility, prayer, and response.
summary.what_was_special: The focus verse concentrates intention, perception, proof, spatial redirection, moral danger, servanthood, and purification into one hinge. Context repeatedly unfolds those compressed terms into architecture, movement, material evidence, social contagion, coercion, and renewed dependence without forcing them into one final reading.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether his هَمَّ denotes equivalent desire, incipient action, reactive movement, or a deliberately suspended threshold remains grammatically unresolved even after the causal asymmetry is clearer.
Whether السوء and الفحشاء distinguish internal inclination from external coercion, sexual act from public exposure, or general harm from exceeded limit remains multiply live.
The identity and mode of the seen برهان remain unspecified; the later shirt-sign clarifies proof function but should not be collapsed into the earlier object.
Imprisonment can be read both as proof's institutional defeat and as a second protective redirection, and the packet does not require choosing between them.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Forming resolve is interrupted by visible proof.** ه م م B001 (resolve forming in the self), ر ء ي B001 (seeing by eye or insight), ب ر ه ن B001 (established proof), and ص ر ف B001 (turning/diverting) supply a directional sequence. The packet states resolve, sight, and diversion; I infer that apprehended proof redirects incipient action. The ayah reads dynamically as altered trajectory, while leaving the two instances of `هم` grammatically distinct.
2. **Diversion acts on both harm and indecency without merging them.** ص ر ف B001 governs س و ء and ف ح ش as coordinated but distinct objects. I infer that one protection blocks harmful consequence and the other blocks boundary-violating act. The paired nouns preserve social and moral dimensions rather than reducing the scene to one category.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:33-34 repeated ص ر ف and كيد in prayer and response, clarifying that diversion was an ongoing protection beyond the single moment of proof.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Incipient resolve under an interrupting condition.** `ه م م:B001` is “resolve forming in the self,” covering intention and self-directed thought. The repeated verb gives formal symmetry, but *lawlā an raʾā* and the following purpose clause supply an interruption; 12:25 then records movement toward the exit, not consummation. The packet gives the two formations of resolve, the seen proof, divine diversion, and flight; I infer that the second trajectory is blocked before becoming the act toward which the first presses. The ayah reads dynamically as resolve encountered and redirected, without merging the two agents’ roles.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:90 identifies guardedness and patience as the durable conditions of the outcome, clarifying that the interrupted resolve here was redirected into a sustained practice rather than erased by one moment.

Kararlılığın yüksek veya düşük oluşu, güçlü kararlılık taşıyan kişi ve bir işi düşünmediğini ya da yapmayacağını bildiren kalıp bu çekirdeğe bağlı özel kullanımlardır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi üzüntü, tasa ve kaygının kişiyi içten yıpratması çekirdeğini açıkça destekler. Kaygı veren çetin iş ve başkasının işiyle ilgilenme kullanımları bu duygusal yükün farklı yönleridir; yalın istek ve karar bu dala girmez.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal zihinsel karar değil, kişiyi üzen, kaygılandıran ve ağır gelen duygusal yük alanıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın dalın üzüntü ve kaygı çekirdeğini verir; başka dallardaki kalıplaşmış ya da maddi erime anlamlarını içeri almaz.

concept_map.definition: Kişiyi içten yıpratan üzüntü, tasa ve kaygıdır. Ağır ve çetin bir işin bu duyguyu doğurması ile bir başkasının işi için kaygılanıp onunla ilgilenme bu çekirdeğe bağlıdır.

facets.statement: Üzüntü, tasa veya kaygı kişiyi içten yıpratır ve huzursuz eder.

Kişi bir başkasının işi için kaygılanabilir ve onun işiyle yakından ilgilenebilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar üzüntü ve kaygının kişiyi eritip yıpratması konusunda birleşir; ağır iş, kaygılandırma ve bir başkasının işiyle ilgilenme kullanımları da aynı duygusal yük çevresinde verilir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesinin ana ekseni bir şeyi eritmek, katı maddenin eriyip gevşemesi ve eriyen maddenin akmasıdır; bu yüzden dal korunabilir. Ancak hastalığın kişiyi tüketmesi, terin akması ve sütün kaba sağılması da aktarılmıştır; bunlar yalnızca katılıktan sonra erime diye tanımlanamaz ve ayrı bağlı kullanımlar olarak tutulmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Katılıktan eriyip akma çekirdektir; hastalıkla tükenme, ter akışı ve kaba süt sağma aynı düzeyde kurucu anlam sayılmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın erime ve eritme alanını temel alır; örnek ve yan kullanımları çekirdeğe karıştırmadan ayrı gösterir.

concept_map.definition: Katı bir maddeyi eritmek veya katı maddenin eriyip gevşeyerek akmasıdır. Hastalığın bedeni tüketmesi, terin akması ve sütün kaba sağılması bu çekirdeğe bağlanan ayrı kullanımlardır.

facets.statement: Isı veya başka bir etki katı maddeyi eritir.
Katı madde eriyip gevşer; ortaya çıkan sıvı akabilir ve erimiş ürün ayrıca adlandırılabilir.
Hastalık bedeni eritip tüketir veya ter alından akıp gider.
Bir aktarımda sütün doğrudan bir kaba sağılması da aynı sözle anlatılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar yağın ve donmuş maddenin eritilmesi, erimesi ve eriyen bölümün akması çekirdeğini paylaşır. Toplu aktarım ayrıca hastalığın bedeni tüketmesini, ter akışını, güneşin karı eritmesini ve sütün kaba sağılmasını içerir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi iki açık adlandırmayı bir araya getirir: suyu çok olan kuyu ve bol su boşaltan bulut. Ortak eksen suyun bolluğudur; erime, hafif yağmur veya yalnızca akış bu dalın kurucu anlamı değildir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal su bolluğunu kuyu ve bol yağış bırakan bulut üzerinden anlatır; sıradan akış veya hafif yağış yeterli değildir.

concept_map.definition: Suyu çok olan kuyu veya bol miktarda yağış boşaltan buluttur. İki kullanımda da ayırt edici özellik suyun ya da yağışın bolluğudur.

Baş biti, yılanın insanı sokması ve deve ya da ata genişletilen tekil kullanım çekirdeğe bağlı örnek ve uzanımlardır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yaşlılıktan tükenmiş, bedeni zayıflamış ve ömrün etkisiyle çökmüş erkek ile kadını açıkça tanımlar. Maddi erime bu dalda benzetme kaynağıdır; hastalık tek başına veya yalnızca yaş sayısının yüksekliği bütün anlamı karşılamaz.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: İleri yaşa bedensel tükenme ve çöküş eşlik eder; dal yalnızca yaşlı olma bilgisinden daha dardır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: İleri yaşın bedenen tükettiği ve belirgin biçimde yıprattığı kadın için kullanılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi ince taneli, hafif ve yumuşak yağmuru ortak çekirdek olarak verir; ayrıca yumuşak esen rüzgâr aynı adlandırmanın ikinci hava kullanımıdır. Bol yağış, sert rüzgâr ve eriyen kar suyu bu sınırın dışındadır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Yağmurda hafiflik ve ince damla, rüzgârda yumuşak esiş belirleyicidir; şiddetli hava olayları kapsanmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın dalın hafif yağmur ve yumuşak rüzgâr kullanımlarını ayırarak verir; birini ötekine genellemez.

concept_map.definition: İnce damlalı, hafif ve yumuşak yağmur veya yumuşak biçimde esen rüzgârdır.

facets.statement: Yağmur hafif, yumuşak ve ince damlalıdır.
Aynı adlandırma yumuşak biçimde esen rüzgâr için de kullanılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar hafif ve yumuşak yağmur anlamını paylaşır; damlaların inceliği ayrıca belirtilir. Toplu aktarımda yumuşak esen rüzgâr da aynı adlandırma altında yer alır.

concept_gloss.text: ince taneli hafif yağmur veya yumuşak esinti

error_profile.preserves: Yağmurun incelik ve hafifliğini, rüzgârın yumuşaklığını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Damlaları küçük, düşüşü hafif ve yumuşak olan yağmur için kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yağmurun ince damlalı, hafif ve yumuşak oluşunu korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Sertlik taşımadan hafif ve yumuşak biçimde esen rüzgâr için kullanılır.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: ince taneli, hafif ve yumuşak yağmur

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal yalnızca yumuşak esişi adlandırır; komşu dal rüzgârın şiddet ve kullanım bakımından geniş alanını kapsar.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal sert, sıcak veya yazın toz taşıyan güçlü rüzgârı anlatır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi göğüste yinelenen boğuk sesi çekirdek olarak açıkça verir. Eşek, sığır, fil ve aslan sesleri, gök gürültüsünün uğultusu, rüzgârın salladığı kamış ve anlaşılmaz insan konuşması bu ses niteliğinin farklı taşıyıcılarıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Belirleyici özellik sesin göğüste veya kapalı bir boşlukta boğuk biçimde yinelenmesidir; sırf yüksek ya da burundan çıkması yetmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın ses çekirdeğini verir ve hayvan, doğa ile insan örneklerini bu çekirdeğe bağlı tutar.

concept_map.definition: Göğüste veya kapalı bir boşlukta yinelenen boğuk, uğultulu ve açık seçik olmayan sestir. Hayvan sesleri, gök gürültüsü, rüzgârla sallanan kamış ve anlaşılmayan insan konuşması bunun örnekleridir.

facets.statement: Ses göğüste veya kapalı bir boşlukta boğuk biçimde yinelenir.
Eşek, sığır, fil ve aslan sesleri ile gök gürültüsü ve rüzgârın salladığı kamış bu sesi çıkarabilir.
Sözleri açık seçik anlaşılmayan insanın boğuk konuşması da aynı ses niteliğiyle anlatılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar sesi göğüste yineleme çekirdeğinde birleşir. Toplu aktarım hayvanların boğuk seslerini, gök gürültüsünün uğultusunu, rüzgârla sallanan kamışı ve açık konuşmayan insanı örnekler.

identity_judgment.rationale: Tek kaynak ifadesi, bir kadının çocuğu uyutmak için ona yumuşattığı ince bir sesle seslenmesini açıkça belirtir. Genel boğuk uğultu, çocuğu sallama ve yatak hazırlama bu eylemin yerine geçmez.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi parmakları saçların arasına sokup ileri geri hareket ettirmeyi ve başı ayıklayıp temizlemeyi açıkça destekler. Uyutma amacı bir örnekte anılsa da eylemin kurucu biçimi saç içinde yinelenen parmak hareketidir.
